what: The Ensign Group runs skilled nursing facilities and senior living communities across the American West and Midwest, operating them under local brands with local management rather than one national chain.
customers: Older patients needing nursing care after hospital stays, paid for by Medicare, Medicaid and insurers.
money: its real estate arm and senior living
moat: A model of buying underperforming facilities and handing them to a local leader with real autonomy, which has turned around hundreds of them and which larger chains have failed to copy.
risks: Medicaid and Medicare rates set most of the revenue and are decided by governments
Nursing wages have risen faster than reimbursement
26 times earnings with free cash flow of only $210M against $399M of net income, because facilities are being bought
opportunities: Revenue grew from $2.6B to $5.1B in four years, nearly doubling
Analysts see about 28% upside, with 5 covering the stock
The over-80 population is growing quickly while almost no new nursing facilities are being built
watch: Occupancy and skilled mix in the facilities acquired in the last two years.
